ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$6.40 (Ryde voucher per NS-7) for the unexempted detour mileage on this metered RydeTAXI trip; note the exemption of the second off-route segment due to the LTA-verified breakdown and the rider's prior chat consent to the PGP routing.

segment_findings.reason: Detour 1 (~10:09–10:17, GPS deviates south of the quoted AYE line to ~1.2879,103.7786 and returns at ~1.2949,103.7852). The driver's chat at 10:06:00 named the alternative ('go round via Prince George's Park') and the rider's own message at 10:06:40 ('Sure, go ahead.') precedes the segment start, so the rider consented before the detour began → no deviation (RD-5).

Detour 2 (~10:17–10:26, GPS runs north via PIE to ~1.3270,103.7454 before rejoining). Not covered by the PGP consent, but the driver's congestion claim is corroborated by the LTA incident 'Vehicle breakdown on Ayer Rajah Expressway' reported 09:47, inside the trip window, ~20 m from the optimal route (≤300 m match) → reason-based exemption (RD-4(a)); AYE speed band 5 on the optimal route is supporting (RD-4(b)).

rejected_claims.reason: Not relied on: driver's statement says the rider agreed verbally / only cites the breakdown. RD-5 requires the rider's own message for consent, and here consent for seg1 is in fact evidenced by the rider's 10:06:40 chat; for seg2 the exemption rests on RD-4, not on any verbal agreement (G11).

Rejected in part: the rider's claim to the whole estimate difference is not granted because both off-route segments are exempt (RD-5 consent for seg1, RD-4 LTA incident for seg2) and only the residual unexplained mileage is refundable on a metered fare (RD-2).
